project_scope.note: Video-fed family teaching reference from Epipactis gigantea. Five Orchidaceae concepts, including E. gigantea, are already installed in the learner; this does not establish target-zone nativity or resolve county-range review.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Find the lip and the column: orchid flowers typically have 3 sepals plus 3 petals, with one petal modified into a labellum (lip), while the fertile sexual structures are consolidated into a column.
family_diagnostics.flower: Usually strongly zygomorphic; the labellum often differs dramatically from the other petals. Many species are resupinate, but resupination is not universal.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Pollen is commonly packaged into pollinia associated with the column rather than released as ordinary loose pollen.
family_diagnostics.ovary: Inferior; in many orchids the ovary or flower stalk twists as the flower develops.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a capsule containing many extremely small seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: A strange-looking flower is not enough. The strongest family package is labellum + column + inferior ovary, with pollinia as a high-value confirmation.
family_diagnostics.vegetative_exceptions: Leafless mycoheterotrophic Corallorhiza wisteriana and the former Hexalectris concepts now mapped to Bletia nitida/B. warnockii lack ordinary green leaves. Do not generalize leaflessness to all Bletia or Orchidaceae. Leafy Epipactis and Spiranthes may have foliage that withers by flowering.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole flower → labellum → column/anther cap → pollinia
visual_lesson.intro: The fastest way to stop orchids from looking mysterious is to read the flower as a set of modified parts rather than as one complicated shape.

steps.title: 1 · Count the flower in threes
steps.photo_role: Epipactis gigantea whole flower / six-part perianth
steps.look_for: Three sepals and three petals arranged around a strongly asymmetric flower.
steps.why_it_matters: This establishes the monocot framework before focusing on the orchid-specific structures.

steps.title: 2 · Find the labellum
steps.look_for: One of the three petals is conspicuously modified into the lip or labellum.
steps.why_it_matters: The labellum is one of the most memorable orchid structures and helps orient the rest of the flower.

steps.title: 3 · Move to the column
steps.look_for: A central column where staminal and stylar tissues are combined instead of appearing as ordinary separate stamens around a free style.
steps.why_it_matters: The column is a much stronger family-level character than flower color or overall showiness.

steps.title: 4 · Expose the pollinia
steps.look_for: Compact pollen masses beneath or associated with the anther cap.
steps.why_it_matters: Pollinia make the orchid reproductive system visually distinct from most superficially similar six-tepaled monocots.

comparisons.title: Orchidaceae vs Asparagaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can present six-part monocot flowers, but orchids combine a specialized labellum with a reproductive column and commonly pollinia; Asparagaceae lacks the orchid column/pollinium package.

comparisons.title: Do not require resupination
comparisons.rule: Many orchid flowers twist during development, but a non-resupinate flower can still be an orchid. Use column, labellum and ovary position instead.

comparisons.title: Orchidaceae vs leafless Orobanchaceae
comparisons.rule: Leaflessness alone is misleading. Orchids show three sepals and three petals including a modified lip, a fused reproductive column and an inferior ovary. Leafless broomrapes generally show a fused corolla, distinct stamens and a superior ovary. Confirm with flower-center and side views; the current learner need not include a leafless broomrape.

visual_lesson.caveat: Epipactis gigantea and four other Orchidaceae concepts are already canonical learner species; their presence does not establish county-native status. genus_routing.look_here_first: Leafy stem, open flower with distinctive labellum and column; inspect inferior ovary separately from flower stalk.
Many small flowers in a spiral or crowded spike; confirm lip and column on an individual flower. Spike twist alone cannot confirm S. cernua.
Leafless, mycoheterotrophic flowering shoot; confirm orchid lip and column on a flower.
Leafless flowering stalk in the represented nitida/warnockii concepts; examine labellum crests and column, not leaflessness alone.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Special lower petal, fused pollen/stigma structure and seed-making chamber below the flower
anatomy_examples.botanical_label: labellum; gynostemium; inferior ovary distinct from pedicel
anatomy_examples.look_for: Pair the same flower's face/center and side views; resolve lip, column and ovary boundaries immediately below perianth. An unopened anther cap does not prove exposed pollinia.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species flower-face and lateral attachment macro
anatomy_examples.caption: Follow the labellum to the column; locate the inferior ovary below the perianth, not the entire flower stalk.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Tiny flowers arranged around the spike; lip and side sepals
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show complete spike and individual open flower; resolve lip and lateral sepals without assuming spiral arrangement identifies species.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species whole spike plus individual flower macro
anatomy_examples.caption: The spike suggests Spiranthes; the individual flower reveals the orchid structures.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Leafless flowering shoot and special lip
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show complete leafless shoot paired with flower-center macro demonstrating lip and column.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species flowering habit and flower-center macro
anatomy_examples.caption: No ordinary green leaves; confirm Orchidaceae with the lip and column.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Raised ridges on the special lower petal and central reproductive structure
anatomy_examples.look_for: Show entire flowering stalk and oblique open-flower macro; verify crest relief and column. Historic source name Hexalectris warnockii is an alias, not a second card.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: exact-species habit and oblique labellum/column macro
anatomy_examples.caption: Look for the crested labellum and column; leaflessness is not universal across Bletia.
